messages.author: dc798b4915310357
messages.subject: Importing own data as.telemetry issue
parts:
Hi, 

I'm fairly new to R and struggling to get to grips with some of the basics of the ctmm package. I've watched some of the training videos online (thank you for making these available to watch, they were great!) and have run the buffalo code succesfully, however I'm having difficulties applying the code to my own data set and getting myself a bit confused using the ctmm package instructions. 

I was hoping someone might be able to help me get my data in the right format to start running the Variogram and AKDE code? I have no uniform sampling strategy so I'm hoping to complete a weighted AKDE. Unfortunatly uploading the data to Movebank is not possible with the data set I'm using.

Currently my table has the following information/headings with one example coordinate included for reference (converted from BNG to WGS84): 
individual.local.identifier / timestamp / location.lat / location.long 
Test / 2019/03/22 00:34:00.00 / -5.169 / 56.514

when I try to run the following code this error occurs: 
test <- read.csv('test_sample.csv')
test <- as.telemetry(test)

Minimum sampling interval of 0 microseconds in Test Warning messages: 1: In telemetry.clean(telist[[i]], id = id[i]) : Times might be out of order or duplicated in Test. Make sure that timeformat and timezone are correctly specified. 2: In telemetry.clean(telist[[i]], id = id[i]) : Duplicate data in Test removed. 3: In telemetry.clean(telist[[i]], id = id[i]) : Duplicate times in Test. Data cannot be fit without an error model.
I can see that someone else has had the same issue previously but I don't know how to make sure my timestamps are correct / use the POSIXct code. It would be great if anyone could help me get that line of code sorted!

Any thoughts or comments are much appreciated, thank you for your help,
Best
Charlotte

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Importing own data as.telemetry issue
parts:
Hi Charlotte,

There are three possible solutions here:
  1. If your timestamps are formatted well enough, then timeformat="auto" may work
  2. Get them into POSIX format, which you can infer from the buffalo data from head(buffalo[[1]])
  3. Provide an appropriate timeformat argument from documentation and examples in help("strptime")
Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Importing own data as.telemetry issue
parts:
Hi Charlotte,

Attempt 1:
t100 <- as.telemetry(t100, timeformat = "auto")

t100 wouldn't be defined yet, so this would error out as written.

But from the warning, you might want to check if your data does, in fact, contain a repeated timestamp. That can happen.

Attempt 2:

As in Attempt 1,  t100 was never initially assigned.

That's the default timezone argument, so the output should be exactly the same as the first attempt if not recycling objects in an unintended way.

I'm not sure what you are doing in attempts 3 & 4, as you are calling format() on the entire data.frame or telemetry object. You would only be formatting timestamps and only after they were imported into POSIX format, so I don't see how that would help in any case.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Importing own data as.telemetry issue
parts:
Hi Charlotte,

It looks like you do have duplicate timestamps in the data. I would check your matching timestamps' location estimates before deleting the duplicates (which will all be the later records), which you can do after import. Sometimes one of the duplicates is way worse than the other.

As you have removed the duplicate timestamps there, the remaining warning implies that your timestamps are out of order. This could be because they are actually out of order or because the non-standard timestamp format isn't importing correctly.

You can either try timeformat="auto", which will will call parsedate to try and infer the format, or you can provide the format by hand, which would look something like timeformat="%d/%m/%Y %H:%M" here.

This is one of the biggest reasons I try to steer users through Movebank, because they have an entire point-and-click interface for getting your timestamps in correctly. On Movebank, your data do not have to be publicly available.

Best,
Chris

On Tue, Jun 13, 2023 at 2:37 PM Christen Fleming <chris.h...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Charlotte,

It looks like you do have duplicate timestamps in the data. I would check your matching timestamps' location estimates before deleting the duplicates (which will all be the later records), which you can do after import. Sometimes one of the duplicates is way worse than the other.

As you have removed the duplicate timestamps there, the remaining warning implies that your timestamps are out of order. This could be because they are actually out of order or because the non-standard timestamp format isn't importing correctly.

You can either try timeformat="auto", which will will call parsedate to try and infer the format, or you can provide the format by hand, which would look something like timeformat="%d/%m/%Y %H:%M" here.

This is one of the biggest reasons I try to steer users through Movebank, because they have an entire point-and-click interface for getting your timestamps in correctly. On Movebank, your data do not have to be publicly available.

Best,
Chris
